Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Sources indicate that willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

It has been revealed that newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

According to recent reports, finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

Double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

Industry observers note that what colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Sources indicate that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Sources indicate that scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Industry observers note that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

Sources indicate that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

The delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

Recent findings suggest that gonzález is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

Recent findings suggest that I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

It has been revealed that first piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

Industry observers note that barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

It has been revealed that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Sources indicate that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

Again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Industry observers note that newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

Recent findings suggest that fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Industry observers note that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

It has been revealed that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the upcoming season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nell’anticipazione dell’intervista, Francesca Fagnani suggerisce la prima parola della sigla latina.

Sources indicate that francesco Totti è alle prese con gli acronimi SPQR e LGBTQIA+ in un’anticipazione della sua intervista a Belve. L’ex capitano della Roma fatica a ricordare il significato della prima sigla e risponde con alcune battute alle domande di Francesca Fagnani sulla seconda. Lo scambio è riportato da Cinemaserietv.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Tra le prime domande dell’anteprima c’è quella su SPQR, l’acronimo latino che compare da secoli sullo stemma di Roma e che per anni è stato presente anche sulle maglie giallorosse. Totti non sembra ricordarne con precisione il significato: «SPQR erano quelle… che era… ‘na cosa che nun me ricordo bene».

In a recent development, fagnani gli suggerisce la prima parola, Senatus. L’ex numero dieci prova a proseguire, poi si ferma: «Senatus? Mo’ pure il latino vuoi… Senatus Popolusco e Romanus so’ troppe frasi».

It has been revealed that la conduttrice passa quindi a LGBTQIA+. Totti sembra non riconoscere l’acronimo e, inizialmente, lo associa alla tecnologia: «LGBT? Nun so’ tecnologico io. LGBTQ Plus. Ma che è, un telefonino?».

Fagnani insiste con la domanda e l’ex calciatore continua sullo stesso tono ironico: «18 Plus? Ma ndo’ le tiri fuori ‘ste domande?. Ma come famo?». Il botta e risposta fa parte delle anticipazioni dell’intervista che Totti concederà alla conduttrice.

L'ASSE dispose d'atouts considérables

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

It has been revealed that "Il y a un changement macroéconomique dans l’industrie du football. L’ère du chef d’entreprise qui veut s’offrir une danseuse en investissant ses fonds propres pour se faire plaisir le week-end est derrière nous. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes dans une logique d’investissement beaucoup plus raisonnée, même si elle laisse toute sa place à la passion. Quand Larry Tannenbaum mandate Ivan Gazidis pour trouver un club de football dans lequel investir, il recherche un actif à fort potentiel sur un marché mûr. Il ne s’agit donc pas du tout de mécénat à fonds perdus. Pour autant, cet investissement porte sur un produit d’émotion, et l’AS Saint-Étienne dispose d’atouts considérables en la matière.

Industry observers note that nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen. Historiquement, nous sommes une des équipes les plus titrées de France et nous bénéficions d’un engouement qui dépasse largement notre territoire. Nos supporters sont répartis dans toute la France et notre fréquentation au stade est totalement décorrélée de notre niveau sportif actuel. Nous affichons la sixième affluence du football français, alors que nous évoluons sportivement en deuxième division.

Pour Kilmer Sport Ventures, l’ASSE présentait des caractéristiques intéressantes mais le club était aussi une sorte de géant endormi qui, ces dernières années, n’avait pas bénéficié des investissements de modernisation nécessaires pour rester compétitif dans le football contemporain. L’idée est donc de réveiller le club grâce à des investissements ciblés, fondés sur une analyse approfondie de l’existant et de nos objectifs afin de repositionner l’AS Saint-Étienne comme une institution, sur le terrain comme en dehors.

Industry observers note that un club de football peut être considéré comme un média. Plus son exposition est forte, dans les médias traditionnels comme sur les réseaux sociaux, plus il peut valoriser son inventaire commercial, c’est-à-dire les espaces qu’il propose à ses sponsors. À l’ASSE, nous bénéficions d’une audience nationale élevée. C’est ce qui nous rend attractifs pour le diffuseur, même en Ligue 2. Nous travaillons aussi à valoriser cette audience sur les réseaux sociaux, où nous rassemblons plus de 2,9 millions de fans sur l’ensemble de nos plateformes.

It has been revealed that aujourd’hui, nous sommes capables de générer en France l’une des 10 plus fortes valorisations médiatiques pour nos annonceurs, et ce malgré notre présence en deuxième division. C’est notamment le fruit du travail mené en communication et en marketing pour faire rayonner l’équipe au-delà du stade.

Sources indicate that L’enjeu, au-delà de la seule billetterie, est de transformer notre notoriété en revenus. Cela passe d’abord par notre ancrage régional. Nous devons continuer à attirer des supporters au stade et à remplir Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais nous devons aussi toucher ceux qui ne peuvent pas venir au stade, en développant notre marque et nos produits dérivés. Cela suppose de travailler notre présence sur les réseaux sociaux, de valoriser les joueurs et de construire leur image, notamment lorsqu’ils sont issus de notre centre de formation. Certains disposent déjà de communautés importantes, capables de contribuer à la vente de maillots et d’ouvrir de nouveaux marchés. À défaut, c’est au club de construire cette visibilité.

Industry observers note that notre ambition est de conquérir de nouveaux publics, notamment en Europe, mais chaque chose en son temps. Notre audience dépasse aujourd’hui notre territoire régional, mais nous ne pouvons pas prétendre rivaliser aujourd’hui avec le PSG à l’échelle internationale. Cela passera d’abord par le retour en Ligue 1 et par des performances sportives à la hauteur de nos ambitions. C’est toute la complexité de notre activité. Nous pouvons bâtir une stratégie marketing solide et développer nos outils de fidélisation, mais les résultats sportifs restent déterminants. Si vous perdez cinq matchs de suite, la dynamique commerciale s’en ressent forcément. Le projet sportif reste le juge de paix, même si nous devons apprendre à développer nos revenus au-delà du seul résultat du week-end.

According to recent reports, la grande différence entre être DAF ou CMO d’une start-up dans la tech et dans un club comme Saint-Etienne ? A mon sens, elle tient à l’attachement des supporters envers le club et à la manière dont il influence leur vie. Très peu d’entreprises peuvent se targuer de voir leur logo tatoué sur le corps d’un de leurs clients et, pourtant, c’est le cas de l’ASSE. En outre, lorsqu’on se promène dans la ville, tous les acteurs économiques et politiques ont un avis sur la situation du club. Dans une région industrielle en difficulté, cette proximité et l’intensité de cette relation sont primordiales pour rassembler la population. Cette intensité m’a vraiment surpris, par comparaison avec les autres entreprises où j’ai travaillé. Le club cristallise des espoirs, des projections de succès qui transcendent le football.".

#107461. Opinion: The morality of football

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1290 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • In a recent development, is football a moral force for good?
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

In a recent development, is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

It has been revealed that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

Industry observers note that in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

It has been revealed that yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

Industry observers note that if humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

To so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

It has been revealed that in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

Recent findings suggest that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

Recent findings suggest that the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise notable questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Sources indicate that défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre. Extraits.

Recent findings suggest that "Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne. J’ai découvert la région, les Stéphanois. Le Forez… qu’est-ce qu’il fait froid là-bas ! C’est dur, la ville c’est compliqué. Tu peux entendre beaucoup de personnes te dire qu’il n’y a rien à faire dans cette ville, que c’est moche, etc. Mais moi j’ai bien aimé Saint-Etienne ! C’est sûr qu’il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire, que tu ne vas pas t’amuser comme si t’étais à Lyon, à Paris ou à Marseille. Mais il y a un p’tit truc, une histoire de fou et tu t’attaches à cette ville. Franchement, j’ai vécu de belles années là-bas ! A Marseille, il y a tellement une histoire forte que quand tu vas parler avec les gens, ils sont fiers de te parler de la ville. C’est beau. Sainté, c’est un peu similaire. Avec le froid en plus mais franchement c’est une superbe ville.

It has been revealed that C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne. Je jouais dans un club très populaire à Marseille qui s'appelle le Sporting Club Air Bel, et il y avait tout le temps des recruteurs car c'est un club qui est connu pour sortir des joueurs pour conduire en centre de formation. J'ai fait beaucoup d'essais, dans presque tous les clubs de France, à part le PSG et les clubs dans le Nord. J’ai fait des essais à Montpellier, Nice, Monaco, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Marseille. J'ai même fait Auxerre. Lyon ? Non. Quand t'es petit, pour aller à Lyon, il faut savoir jouer au ballon. Moi, j'étais trop un boucher !

In a recent development, la première fois que j'ai fait un essai à Saint-Etienne, ils ne m'ont pas pris à la base, ils m'ont dit, « on va te revoir », la fameuse phrase « On te rappellera. » Mais ils sont revenus me voir quand je jouais avec Air Bel, et ils m'ont refait faire un essai. Et après cet essai, ils m'ont dit :  « c'est bon, on va te garder ». Quand j’arrive là-bas, c'est compliqué. En fait, t'arrives et il y a des règles, des codes, des trucs que tu ne peux pas faire. Et moi, quand j'étais petit, c'était un peu : si je veux faire un truc, je veux le faire. Et d'où je viens, il n'y a pas réellement... Ce n'est pas qu'il n'y a pas de règles, parce que ce ne serait pas bien de dire qu'il n'y a pas de règles. Parce que j'ai été éduqué, j'ai eu une bonne éducation, mais ce n'est pas pareil. Les règles, tu peux les contourner. Pour nous, les règles, si on n'est pas d'accord avec la règle, on va la contourner. Un peu de filouterie, voilà.

It has been revealed that sauf qu'au centre de formation, ça ne passe pas. Et après, t'arrives, t'es dans un centre avec d'autres jeunes, des gens de ton âge, des gens qui jouent à ta place. Et c'est un peu la « guerre » parce qu'il y a des gens qui jouent à ta place, mais toi, t'es là, tu les regardes, t'as envie de jouer. C'est la concurrence, c'est comme ça. Mais oui, c'était un peu compliqué. Surtout, je quittais Marseille, j'arrivais à Saint-Etienne. Au début, je me suis dit « Mais qu'est-ce que je fous ici ? Qu'est-ce que je vais faire dans cette ville de fous ? » Un truc tout bête, tu sors dehors, c'est où qu'on peut aller grailler, c'est où qu'on peut aller manger ? Tu regardes les grecs, les snacks, il n'y a rien qui va. Tu veux aller te faire couper les cheveux, il n'y a rien qui va. Mais après, petit à petit, tu trouves les petites adresses, les connexions et j’étais bien. Tu rencontres des Stéphanois là-bas, ils te disent « T'inquiète, va ici, va là ».

Sources indicate that franchement, au centre de formation, il y avait du niveau. Je pense qu'il y avait des jeunes en U17, U19, même en réserve, qui étaient « destinés » à du très, très haut niveau, mais qui n'ont jamais réussi à aller le chercher. Après, les Stéphanois, ils sont très fiers et ils ont des grosses valeurs. C'est ça, surtout, qu'on nous a appris. La valeur que le club, il a dans la ville, ça, on le comprend très jeune. Parce que les gens de là-bas, ils vivaient un peu à travers le club. Quand ça gagne le week-end, ils sont très contents. Quand ça perd, ils sont un peu tristes. Et dans la ville, tu le ressens. Le centre de formation, ce n’est que des bons souvenirs. On a fait beaucoup de bêtises, les directeurs du centre voulaient notre peau plus d'une fois. On va dire qu'ils ont des anecdotes. C'est des super souvenirs et on avait de belles générations. Franchement, moi, j'ai connu 98-99, ma génération 2000, 2001, 2002. Franchement, il y a eu des gros joueurs qui sont sortis. Il y a eu de très, très beaux joueurs.

C’est là que j’ai connu William Saliba. On  joué ensemble de U17 jusqu'à U19. On a gagné la Gambardella ensemble. Ouais, j'allais en parler. Même si il n'a pas joué la finale, on a gagné la Gambardella parce qu'on a joué la compétition ensemble. Et après, on a joué pendant un an, un an et demi ensemble. Lui, il est monté très vite en pro. On a joué en pro ensemble. Avec William, c'est une belle histoire parce qu'on a commencé très, très jeunes et on s'est retrouvés en pro ensemble. On a grandi ensemble et on est toujours en contacts même si on joue dans des clubs rivaux. Je le connais par cœur, il me connait par cœur. C'est la famille. On n'a pas besoin de se parler tous les jours mais on va se parler de temps en temps. On va se parler et après, quand on se voit, il n'y a rien qui bouge. C’est beau qu’on ait gardé ça. Parce qu'au-delà du fait qu'on ait grandi ensemble, qu'on soit arrivé au « sommet » ensemble, on joue au même poste. Ça aurait pu affecter notre relation mais depuis jeune, ça n'a jamais touché notre relation. On n'a jamais été affecté par ça, par la concurrence. Même quand on est arrivé en pro, il y a eu beaucoup de trucs qui nous ont mis en compétition, etc. Mais nous, ça ne nous a jamais rien fait. On s'en foutait. Nous, on voulait jouer ensemble, on voulait s'amuser et on voulait le meilleur pour l'autre,.

It has been revealed that quand tu gagnes la Gambardella, t'es un peu la meilleure équipe de jeunes de France. Donc, c'était déjà quelque chose d'incroyable. Au lendemain de notre sacre en Gambardella, on fait un tour d'honneur à Geoffroy-Guichard. Je n'ai jamais fait de banc en pro à ce moment-là, rien ! On fait un tour d'honneur et trois semaines après, je suis sur le banc et il y a une blessure. Et le coach se retourne vers moi et il me fait rentrer arrière-droit contre Alain Saint-Maximin. La première chose que tu as en tête, c'est « il va me salir ». Parce qu'Allan, il est connu pour dribbler, pour salir les gens. Mais après, franchement, sur le moment, je rentre et moi, j'ai qu'un truc en tête, je me dis que chaque fois qu'il touche la balle, il faut que je le monte en l'air. Juste avant de rentrer, je vois l’entraîneur de Nice Patrick Vieira qui fait un geste demandant à ses joueurs d’attaquer de mon côté. Ça te met une petite bouffée de pression. Mais mon coach - enfin, c'était l'adjoint à ce moment-là -  m’a glissé deux ou trois mots avant de rentrer. Julien Sablé m’a dit : « tu joue simple, agressif, tu n’inventes rien , fais ce que tu sais faire. Tu castagnes, tu te bats, tu mets des tacles, des tampons. ». Je n’avais que ça en tête, simple, agressif. Ça s'est bien passé. Bon match, 3-0, première entrée, clean sheet.

It has been revealed that J’enchaîne la semaine d'après, c'est le dernier match de la saison, à Angers. Ma première titu. C’était facile car il n'y avait plus rien à jouer pour les deux équipes. C’était un super match, j’ai kiffé. C'était Jean-Louis Gasset, le coach. Tout le monde le connaît, c'est un mec simple. Et c'était une personne incroyable. J'ai appris beaucoup, beaucoup avec lui et avec son staff. Je n’en garde que de bons souvenirs. C'est sûr que je ne l'ai pas connu aussi longtemps que je l'aurais espéré parce que je n'étais pas réellement avec les pros. Je m'entraînais, mais je n'étais pas réellement avec eux. Ma première apparition en pro j’ai joué latéral mais franchement, je déteste ce poste. Après, comme je l'ai toujours dit, en vrai, tu ne décides pas trop. Tu vas jouer, surtout à cet âge-là, où on va te mettre. Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire ? Tu joues en pro, c’est déjà bien. Sois content, joue tes matchs, fais ton job et après, tu verras. Après, quand tu auras acquis de l'expérience, que  tu auras joué des matchs, tu pourras dire « moi, je préfère, je préfère ci, je préfère ça ». Quand tu es jeune, tu joues où on te met. On m'aurait même mis à gauche ou gardien, c'est bon, j’y serais allé.

In a recent development, je ne l'avais pas en moi, cette qualité de relance mais ça compte, surtout dans le football de maintenant. Ça compte de fou, ça compte énormément. Jouer au ballon, je n'avais pas ça en moi. C'est mon coach, Julien Sablé, que j'ai eu à Saint-Etienne qui m’a fait travailler ça. C'est lui qui m'a rendu fou et qui a pris des heures et des heures avec moi à me dire qu'il faut que la passe soit comme ça, qu'elle soit claquée, qu'il faut jouer dans ces intervalles-là. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué tout ça. Moi, à la base, moi, en tant que défenseur, mon job, et vraiment, j'ai grandi comme ça, c'était : « tu défends, te ne prends pas de but. On s'en fout à qui tu fais la passe. Quand tu as la balle dans les pieds, tu donnes à ton 6, ton arrière-droit. Ils se débrouillent. Eux, c'est leur job de faire le jeu, de s'amuser avec le ballon. » Moi mon plaisir c'était les tampons, les tacles, gagner mes duels, notamment de la tête. Et c'est après, petit à petit, en faisant des séances, des vidéos, etc., en prenant du temps sur le terrain, petit à petit que j'ai commencé à apprécier cet aspect du foot avec le ballon, et j'ai compris beaucoup de choses.

J’ai fait ma première année en pro dans une équipe qui subissait et prenait beaucoup de buts. Tu subis beaucoup, donc tu défends beaucoup, tu es beaucoup exposé. En tant que défenseur, quand tu es jeune et que tu es beaucoup exposé et que tu défends beaucoup, on parle plus de toi, on te voit plus. Par exemple, on allait plus parler de moi qu'on allait parler des attaquants. Parce qu'on ne faisait que défendre et qu’on ne marquait pas beaucoup de buts. Et même quand on en prenait des buts, c'était souvent, « heureusement qu'il est là, sinon on en aurait pris plus ». Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu es défenseur et que ton équipe prend beaucoup de buts, tu passes des mauvais matchs, tu passes des mauvaises soirées. Tu vas jouer à l'extérieur, tu rentres chez toi, t'en as pris trois. Domicile, le week-end d'après, tu reçois, t'es as pris deux. Tu enchaînes les défaites, t’en prends 4, tu perds 5-1. C'est chaud, ce n'est pas un plaisir. Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu n'en prends pas, c'est multiplié fois 20 comparé à d'autres défenseurs ou à d'autres équipes du championnat. Franchement, c'était dur. Mais d'un autre côté, vu que tu défends beaucoup, tu es exposé pour un défenseur et à mon âge, c'était tout bénef pour moi.

Industry observers note that je fais cette finale de Coupe de France contre le PSG. Je fais un très bon match, mais malheureusement on perd la finale. Après cette finale, il y a un peu tout qui s'accélère. Il y a beaucoup de clubs qui s’intéressent à moi. Franchement, Leicester n’était pas là au début. Pour dire la vérité, à la base, moi, c'est Milan AC. Il y a un appel avec les dirigeants, avec Maldini. Maldini, c'est stylé. Quand il te parle et te dit « je vais te prendre sous mon aile » , j’ai envie de lui dire  « emmène-moi, je signe ce que tu veux. » Au départ, avec mes agents et tout mon entourage, on penche plutôt pour le Milan AC.

Industry observers note that après, ça ne se fait pas avec Saint-Etienne parce que d'un côté, Saint-Etienne ne voulait pas me vendre. Mais d'un autre côté, ils étaient un peu dans l'obligation de me vendre par rapport à des problèmes d'argent, etc. Ils étaient un peu entre deux. Ils essaient un peu de faire remonter les enchères. On sait comment ça marche. Milan a monté jusqu'à une limite où ils ont dit « Ça ne sera plus possible. » Et il y a Leicester qui s'est ramené. Leicester, ça a été tout droit. J'ai parlé avec le coach, j'ai parlé avec Kolo Touré qui était dans le staff. Son discours m’a rassuré et mis en confiance. Ensuite, ce n’était pas compliqué. Leicester a fait une offre. Saint-Etienne était d'accord, mais après il y a eu ce problème avec Claude Puel, qui ne voulait vraiment pas me vendre. Mais au final, pour la santé du club, pour le bien du club, il n'avait pas trop le choix. Donc j’ai filé à Leicester l’avant-dernier jour du mercato.".

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

According to recent reports, cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is at the moment playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

His son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

In a recent development, kenneth Taylor vuole restare alla Lazio a gennaio e il club pensa a un ritocco del suo ingaggio. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, il centrocampista ha rassicurato Gattuso dopo l’interesse arrivato dalla Premier League e dalla Juventus. La società intende occuparsi prima dei contratti in scadenza nel 2028, poi affrontare anche la sua situazione.

It has been revealed that durante la sosta della scorsa settimana a Formello, Rino era in allarme per le sirene del mercato. Sono bastate poche parole di Taylor per tranquillizzarlo. Il giocatore gli ha confermato l’interesse ricevuto: «È tutto vero, i miei agenti mi hanno informato.» Gli ha però chiarito che non intende partire a gennaio: «Ma ho già detto che a gennaio non ci penso proprio ad andare via.».

Taylor ha espresso a Gattuso anche il suo obiettivo: «Voglio restare qui e aiutare la Lazio a tornare in Champions». Il tecnico non si aspettava questa risposta e ne è stato molto felice. La Lazio vuole ricompensarlo per l’attaccamento mostrato e per aver rinunciato a guadagni più alti offerti altrove.

Recent findings suggest that dopo aver affrontato i contratti in scadenza nel 2028, il club parlerà di un possibile adeguamento per Kenneth, che percepisce 1,7 milioni di euro fino al 2030. A febbraio riceverà il secondo premio fedeltà da 190mila euro, dopo aver scelto per la seconda volta di restare in biancoceleste. Acquistato dall’Ajax per meno di 17 milioni di euro, con il club olandese che conserva il 10% su una futura rivendita, Taylor si è rivelato un colpo straordinario per la Lazio.

Zohran Mamdani squared off with Upcoming York media and now the city's mayor will need a few months to recover.

As he revealed Friday while announcing prepares to replace Rikers Island jail, Mamdani was playing in a soccer match against the local press corps at an indoor pitch in lower Manhattan when he tore his right Achilles tendon. Consequently, Mamdani is now using crutches and a walking boot, which he expects to be in for the next six to eight weeks.

'I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch and I forgot that I was 35,' Mamdani told gathered media on Friday at City Hall, where he was forced to rely on crutches.

Mamdani hopes to be back playing soccer again in nine months.

Local media may not be to blame here. As Mamdani told the New York Post, he arrived late to the game and began playing without properly stretching. What's more, the Post reported that Mamdani was overheard asking his police guards which reporter tackled him, only to be told he went down untouched.

Despite Mamdani's injury, team City Hall beat the local media, 8-4.

Industry observers note that as he revealed Friday while announcing plans to close Rikers Island, Mamdani was playing  against the local press corps when tore his Achilles. Now he's in a boot (pictured).

Zohran Mamdani and wife Rama Duwaji are seen during a Brazil-Morocco World Cup match.

In a recent development, born in Uganda and raised in Manhattan's Morningside Heights neighborhood, Mamdani played cricket and soccer in his youth. He even suited up for Bowdoin College's JV team during his days at the Maine school. Then later, as an adult, he became a shareholder of Spanish second-division club Real Oviedo.

But his biggest impact on the sport came over the summer, when New York welcomed thousands of tourists for the World Cup action at MetLife Stadium in nearby East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Upset with ticket prices for the matches, Mamdani organized more than 100 free watch parties around the city. The events were well attended and helped locals engage with the tournament even though no actual matches were played in New York.

Zohran Mamdani, center, joined by, from left, United States soccer star Tim Weah NYC World Cup Czar Maya Handa, and New York council member Yusef Salaam back in May.

'We remarked from the beginning that the World Cup belongs to New Yorkers. This summer, we proved it,' Mamdani said in a statement. 'In the most international city on earth, you didn't need thousands of dollars to be part of the world's game.

Industry observers note that 'A kid in Corona, a nurse in Bay Ridge and a small business owner in Little Haiti could all celebrate together — for free or at a price they could afford,' he continued. 'That's what we mean when we talk about a city for the many.

'This summer, strangers became neighbors on Open Streets and in free Fan Fests across the city because government made room for people to come together. And long after the confetti is swept away, Fresh Yorkers will keep what we built: safer streets, faster buses, stronger protections, closer neighbors and the memory of a summer when the whole world felt at home here.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances.
  • "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout.
  • Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

"L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout. Au-delà de sa dimension financière, il s’agit avant tout d’un investissement patrimonial, dans un club qui fait partie du patrimoine français, voire européen. L’AS Saint-Étienne bénéficie d’une résonance internationale, notamment grâce à son histoire et à ses parcours européens dans les années 1970.

Recent findings suggest that cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités. La première concerne évidemment les équipes professionnelles, féminines comme masculines. La seconde porte sur les infrastructures, avec la volonté d’améliorer le centre d’entraînement et de poursuivre la modernisation du stade, en collaboration avec la Métropole de la ville. Enfin, le dernier axe, me semble crucial, car il reflète profondément l’ADN du club : c’est celui de la formation. L’académie doit permettre d’accompagner les jeunes aussi bien dans leur parcours footballistique que dans leur éducation afin de les préparer au mieux à une éventuelle carrière professionnelle.

Sources indicate that la baisse des droits télévisés ne signifie pas nécessairement qu’évoluer en Ligue 2 soit moins intéressant financièrement qu’en Ligue 1. Pour un club de Ligue 1 qui ne dispute pas de compétition européenne et se situe dans la deuxième partie du classement, les revenus audiovisuels peuvent être comparables à ceux d’un club de Ligue 2 de première partie de tableau, alors que les charges salariales sont généralement plus élevées dans l’élite. En échangeant récemment avec plusieurs directeurs administratifs et financiers de clubs de Ligue 1, nous avons constaté que les revenus audiovisuels d’un club classé dans le top 3 de Ligue 2 pouvaient être proches de ceux d’un club occupant la 15e place de Ligue 1.

In a recent development, L’enjeu est ailleurs. La Ligue 1 offre une meilleure valorisation des joueurs. Pour générer des revenus sur le marché des transferts, nous devons donc retrouver l’élite et y réaliser de bonnes performances. Cela vaut aussi bien pour les joueurs que nous recrutons et développons que pour ceux issus de notre centre de formation. Le trading de joueurs constitue ainsi un levier essentiel de notre équilibre financier.

Industry observers note that en parallèle, nous devons optimiser nos coûts d’exploitation et mieux valoriser nos actifs. C’est tout l’intérêt des investissements dans les infrastructures, autour du stade comme au centre de formation. En offrant aux joueurs de meilleures conditions d’entraînement et de développement, nous augmentons leur potentiel de performance et, à terme, leur valeur sur le marché. Ces investissements doivent donc être considérés comme un moyen de renforcer notre capacité à générer des revenus futurs.".

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

Industry observers note that but in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

It has been revealed that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Belahyane viene paragonato ad Almeyda, mentre Mandas richiama Marchegiani per le qualità tra i pali e nelle uscite.

Recent findings suggest that la Lazio di Gattuso ha raccolto nelle prime dodici giornate più punti di quella del 2000, considerata tra le più forti della storia biancoceleste per l’organico al completo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Da quando la vittoria vale tre punti, soltanto la Juventus, prima con Capello e poi con Allegri, ha fatto meglio. È da questi numeri che Il Messaggero parte per accostare le due squadre, pur tenendo distinte le rispettive epoche.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that rino, Frattesi e gli altri biancocelesti continuano a guardare al traguardo dei 40 punti, indicato come quota della salvezza matematica. Dopo la vittoria sul Lecce, il tecnico calabrese aveva spiegato: «E dopo parleremo di altro, con maggiore tranquillità».

Il confronto con la squadra del secondo scudetto riguarda anche lo spogliatoio. Gattuso vi ha portato un clima che richiama, con le dovute proporzioni, quello creato da Eriksson ventisei anni fa. Nella Lazio di allora, però, l’armonia non era quella di oggi: convivevano il gruppo degli ex Samp, guidato da Roberto Mancini, e quello degli argentini, senza un capo designato ma rappresentato dalle personalità di Veron e Simeone.

Il paragone suggerito dalla partita contro il Lecce è quello tra Belahyane e Almeyda. Il marocchino intercetta palloni e li sottrae agli avversari commettendo raramente fallo, come faceva l’argentino. Almeyda era chiamato Capitan Uncino per il modo in cui usava il piede destro per portare via il pallone; Belahyane si affida invece alla rapidità della corsa e all’appoggio del corpo sul rivale per interrompere l’azione.

Tra i portieri, Mandas richiama Luca Marchegiani: entrambi efficaci tra i pali, dotati di personalità sulle palle alte e meno talentuosi nel gioco con i piedi. A Marchegiani costò il posto in Nazionale un errore che Sacchi non gli perdonò.

A centrocampo, Frattesi ricorda Nedved quando arriva nei pressi dell’area pronto a colpire. Il ceco era un attaccante aggiunto per Zoff ed Eriksson; Davide è l’incursore della squadra di Gattuso. Alcuni movimenti di Taylor richiamano Stankovic, più potente soprattutto nel tiro dalla distanza. L’olandese viene accostato anche a Simeone per la capacità di contribuire con gol e assist senza dare nell’occhio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'est confié à Sportfin France. Extraits.

According to recent reports, "La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant. Je préfère utiliser le terme d'héritage, et un héritage, on construit dessus, on ne peut pas renier qui on est. Ça, c'est un présupposé de base. On est un club de foot d'origine populaire qui s'est construit sur une région populaire avec une classe ouvrière très forte. Saint-Etienne, c'est une région qui était minière, qui avait une industrie sidérurgique développée, etc. et qui s'est développée autour de cette industrie. Une industrie qui a depuis périclité. On a un héritage, un héritage minier, un héritage ouvrier, et de ça, aujourd'hui, dans la marque, comme dans le comportement des employés, comme dans le comportement des joueurs, on a encore des traits qui sont très forts. Il y a cette valorisation de la notion de travail. Ici il est attendu, et on le voit dans les tribunes, nos ultras, n'ont de cesse que de le répéter, il faut mouiller le maillot. C'est une expression qui est devenue consacrée, qu'on utilise comme ça, mais les premiers joueurs de l'AS Saint-Etienne, c’étaient des gens qui sortaient de la mine et qui venaient jouer au foot. Pour eux, mouiller le maillot, ce n'était pas une image, c'était une vraie attente. Et aujourd'hui, on a cet héritage-là. Donc, aujourd'hui, oui, quand on regarde sur le passé, ça a créé quelque chose de fantastique.

Le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers. Donc, on est le club que tout le monde regarde à la télé, on devient la marque de football français qui plus en gagne. C'est à une époque où le football français n'avait pas gagné depuis des décennies. Alors, on gagne jusqu'à la finale à Glasgow contre le Bayern de Munich où les fameux poteaux carrés empêchent les Dominique Rocheteau, les Jean-Michel Larqué et Jacques Santini de remporter la Ligue des champions. Mais c'est une équipe qui domine, elle a 10 titres de champion de France dans cette période-là. Donc, on est le club de foot qu'on découvre à la télé, en même temps qu'on découvre à la télé. C'est un club qui gagne, donc on s'y associe et du coup, on établit une marque très très forte, un lien émotionnel très fort. Aujourd'hui, quand on dit les Verts, dans l'inconscient collectif de partout en France, c'est forcément Saint-Etienne. Il y a un lien très fort qui émane de là, donc on ne peut pas renier ce lien-là.

Pour autant, il ne faut pas s'y enfermer parce que sinon, on n'est pas un club de foot, on est un musée. Or aujourd'hui, les ambitions du club, c'est de retrouver ce statut sportif et de faire en sorte que l'institution et sa performance sportive soient mises en corrélation. Aujourd'hui, il y a très peu de clubs qui sont dans cette adéquation. Le Paris Saint-Germain a réussi à aligner le statut du club avec sa performance sportive. Mais quand on est par exemple, en Angleterre, un pays que je connais bien, on a des institutions du football qui ont des vraies difficultés sportives. Et pourtant, ils restent des entités respectées, reconnues comme des clubs monolithiques dans lesquels on doit un respect, une reconnaissance. Je pense à Chelsea par exemple, qui a beaucoup de mal sportivement, ils n'ont pas gagné un titre depuis des années, et pourtant… Manchester United est dans le même acabit.

According to recent reports, nous, on a cette ambition de valoriser cet héritage, de construire dessus, mais en se tournant vers l'avenir. Donc oui, on mettra en avant les Verts 76, on l'a fait l'année dernière pour le cinquantenaire de la finale de Glasgow, et on continuera de mettre en avant d'autres générations au fur et à mesure, parce que c'est sur leurs exploits qu'on a construit là où on est, mais on est définitivement tourné vers l'avenir plutôt que la glorification du passé.

It has been revealed that du design à sa sortie, comment naît un maillot ? Déjà, c'est un travail collectif, dans lequel l'équipementier joue un rôle prépondérant. On a la chance, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, de travailler avec un équipementier qui s'appelle Hummel, avec lequel on a une relation de partenariat. Ce n'est pas toujours le cas, il y a certaines marques qui imposent au club « voilà votre maillot ». Nous, on a la chance d'être en partenariat avec Hummel et de travailler avec eux à la définition de ce maillot. Du coup, on est partie prenante du début jusqu'à la fin.

C'est un process qui dure presque 18 mois. C'est-à-dire qu'aujourd'hui, on a des conversations sur les maillots pas de la saison prochaine mais de la saison d'après. On recherche, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, des designs qui soient à la fois respectueux des codes historiques, pour cette frange de nos fans qui sont très attachés aux valeurs traditionnelles du club. On cherche aussi à pousser les limites dans d'autres secteurs. Ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on cherchera toujours à avoir un maillot qui soit portant de sens. Donc, on va faire des références à notre territoire, à nos supporters, au club.

Cette année, par exemple, le maillot 26-27 fait référence au premier titre de champion de France avec un design qui fait écho à celui de 1966-1967, quand le club est devenu pour la première fois champion de France, avec des bandes larges, un col blanc très large. Et quand on regarde le maillot de près, il y a un logo ASS Saint-Étienne [sic], irisé, qui apparaît, qui est le logo de l'époque. On a travaillé justement il y a un an et demi avec les designers de Hummel pour que ce produit, ce design, ce matériau soient celui-là, et que 18  mois plus tard, on puisse le révéler au public.

C'est quelque chose qui dure 18 mois, une collaboration entre le club d'un côté, avec ses différents services, les personnes qui sont en charge de la commercialisation, qui ont un bon ressenti des produits qui vont se vendre, l'équipe marque qui va réfléchir à « est-ce que le produit enrichit la marque, fait référence à des éléments de la marque qu'on veut à soi ? », mais aussi la partie designer-produit plutôt chez Hummel. Et cette collaboration nous a permis de développer des produits qui répondent vraiment aux attentes de nos fans. Et on a vu une augmentation radicale du nombre de maillots qu'on a vendus. On a multiplié par trois nos volumes de maillots en cinq ans, grâce à cette collaboration prolifique avec Hummel.

Cédric Chambaz vient donc de gagner une invitation au Musée des Verts. Il y découvrira que l'ASSE a en réalité décroché son premier titre de champion de France en 1956-1957. C'est à cette saison-là, magnifiée par la fameuse attaque mitraillette Rijvers-Mekhloufi, Njo Lea, que fait bien sûr référence le maillot porté par les protégés de Ian Cathro.

Published: 14:02 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 03:42 EST, 21 November 2026.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea, according to ESPN.

It would see the seven-time Super Bowl champion make a swift return to investment in English football after he stepped away from Championship leaders Birmingham City earlier this month.

Brady was in attendance at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey when Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

The Newly introduced England Patriots icon, who also owns a minority stake in the NFL's Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly has a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, who oversees the club’s Clearlake Capital ownership.

Chelsea declined to comment when approached, but sources have stood up the negotiations.

Sources indicate that brady, the greatest quarterback of all time, secured a minority stake in Birmingham in August 2023. That followed Tom Wagner purchasing a 45 percent stake at the club earlier that same year.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea.

Brady watched Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

At Birmingham, Brady made headlines when he questioned Wayne Rooney’s work ethic during a documentary following his time at St Andrew’s.

Rooney, who went on to be sacked after just 15 games in charge, later described those comments as ‘very unfair’.

When Brady exited Birmingham, the club noted in a statement: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’.

Chelsea have invited minority shareholders with their women’s team.

NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo previously purchased a stake in the side, partnering with Alexis Ohanian, the founder of social media platform Reddit who likewise invested in the team in 2025.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

Industry observers note that they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

Industry observers note that there is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a fresh City, different personnel and even a new look.

In a recent development, they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

According to recent reports, “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a latest team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are newly introduced to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

In a recent development, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Industry observers note that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca remarked. “This demonstrates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

In a recent development, by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

In a recent development, man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

Industry observers note that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the significant stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

Industry observers note that for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

In a recent development, in probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

Veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Industry observers note that manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Sources indicate that porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

With it hammering down, Porto boss Francesco Farioli has swapped his lovely suit that he was wearing pre-game for a tracksuit top and cap. At half-time, he will probably head back in drenched like all the players if he is active in his dugout.

According to recent reports, we are under way at the Estádio do Dragão with the rain still teaming down in Porto. Manchester City’s Champions League campaign gets going.

It has been pouring down in Porto but that has not dampened the spirits of the home fans, who are in fine voice ahead of kick-off. The pyrotechnics have gone off and it is loud inside the Dragão.
